reason: Rails builds `OpenSSL::Cipher.new` before `generate_iv` (aes256_gcm.rb:38-43) only so `generate_iv` can ask that object for `random_iv`; Node's `createCipheriv` takes the IV as a constructor argument, so the IV must be produced first and the two calls necessarily swap order.

aes256_gcm.rb:94 `OpenSSL::HMAC.digest(OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.new, @secret, clear_text)` is one-shot; node's HMAC is streaming, so the same three arguments land on `createHmac("sha256", key).update(clearText).digest()` (aes256-gcm.ts:163-166) and `digest` itself takes none. Language shortcoming.
`OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.new` (aes256_gcm.rb:95) names the digest as an object; Node's `createHmac("sha256", key)` names it as a string argument, so there is no constructor call to make.
